title: Build System & CI/CD

real_issues.title: Cross-compilation mock includes real Haiku private headers on non-Haiku
real_issues.description: The non-Haiku CXXFLAGS still includes `/boot/system/develop/headers/private/...` paths which only exist on Haiku. These will cause build failures or pull wrong headers on macOS/Linux. The mock_headers should fully replace private headers.

real_issues.title: Duplicate test_expected entry in TEST_BINS
real_issues.description: `test_expected` appears twice in TEST_BINS list (lines 176 and 185). This wastes build time and could mask failures if the first runs but second fails differently.

real_issues.title: Hardcoded Homebrew paths in cross-compilation flags
real_issues.description: `-I/opt/homebrew/include` and `-L/opt/homebrew/lib` assume macOS ARM Homebrew prefix. Fails on Linux, macOS Intel (/usr/local), or custom prefixes. Should use pkg-config or CMake find_package.

real_issues.title: Package target depends on build-addon but not systemone_server
real_issues.description: `package` target lists `systemone_server` as dependency but doesn't ensure it's built before copying. The `build-addon` rule is separate from the main binary dependencies.

real_issues.title: No debug/release build configuration
real_issues.description: CXXFLAGS hardcodes `-O2`. No `make debug` or `CXXFLAGS=-O0 -g` override. Developers must edit Makefile to debug. Standard practice: `BUILD_TYPE ?= release` with conditional flags.

real_issues.title: Haiku private headers used directly instead of public SDK
real_issues.description: Build uses `-I/boot/system/develop/headers/private/...` extensively. Private headers are unstable across Haiku versions. Should prefer public headers + feature detection.

real_issues.title: MD4C source bundled instead of system library
real_issues.description: MD4C (markdown parser) is compiled from `md4c/md4c.c` bundled in-tree. Should use Haiku's `md4c` package if available, or at least vendor it in a `third_party/` dir with license tracking.

real_issues.title: Clean target misses mock library artifacts
real_issues.description: `clean` removes binaries and .o/.d files but not `mock_libs/*.dylib` or `mock_headers/` generated files. Cross-compilation artifacts persist.
real_issues.evidence: clean: rm -f Pluto_cli Pluto systemone_server $(TEST_BINS) bench pluto.rsrc 'Ask pluto' ... (line 377)

real_issues.title: CMake cross-compilation uses INTERFACE libraries for Haiku deps but no mock implementations
real_issues.description: CMake declares `be`, `network`, `tracker`, `translation` as INTERFACE IMPORTED libraries with only include dirs. No mock implementations provided for linking — will fail at link time on non-Haiku.

real_issues.title: Installer script version hardcoded (0.6.0) while project is 0.7.1
real_issues.description: Installer header says `Pluto 0.6.0` but Makefile and recipes show 0.7.1. Version drift between install script and actual release.
real_issues.evidence: # Pluto 0.6.0 installer for Haiku (line 2), echo "Installing Pluto 0.6.0..." (line 14)

real_issues.title: Cross-compilation toolchain assumes fixed SDK path /opt/haiku-sdk
real_issues.description: CMAKE_SYSROOT hardcoded to `/opt/haiku-sdk`. This path varies by installer (HaikuPorts, manual, Docker). Should be configurable via env var or CMake cache.

real_issues.title: systemone_server only links json.o, missing core dependencies
real_issues.description: System One server builds with only `src/json.o` but likely needs config, provider, MCP client, tools, etc. This will fail at link time or produce incomplete binary.

real_issues.title: No test discovery or parallel execution
real_issues.description: `make check` runs 21 test binaries sequentially with `for t in $(TEST_BINS); do ./$$t || exit 1; done`. No parallelization (`make -j`), no test filtering, no JUnit/XML output for CI integration.
real_issues.evidence:
check: $(TEST_BINS)
	@for t in $(TEST_BINS); do echo "==> $$t"; ./$$t || exit 1; done (Makefile lines 344-346)

real_issues.title: HaikuPorts recipe BUILD() just calls `make $jobArgs` — no configure step
real_issues.description: Recipe assumes Makefile works out-of-the-box. No `./configure` or `cmake` step. If Makefile needs environment setup (pkg-config paths, SDK selection), build will fail in clean buildroot.

real_issues.title: Mock headers incomplete — only 82 headers vs thousands in real Haiku SDK
real_issues.description: Mock headers cover only types and classes directly used by Pluto. Any new Haiku API usage requires manual mock addition. No automated generation from Haiku headers.
real_issues.evidence: ls mock_headers/haiku/ | wc -l → 82 headers (vs ~2000+ in real SDK)

hypothetical_findings.description: Makefile has grown organically without modularization — 387 lines of flat rules. Veterans would extract per-target .mk includes, variable files, and use pattern rules for the 21 test binaries.
examples: CORE_SRCS/CORE_OBJS/CLI_OBJS/GUI_OBJS duplicated logic
No automatic dependency generation for new .cpp files
Test binaries each need manual entry in TEST_BINS and explicit rule

hypothetical_findings.description: Zero integration tests, zero end-to-end tests, zero fuzzing. Only 21 unit test binaries testing isolated functions. No test for: CLI REPL, GUI tabs, MCP client, System One tools, Tracker add-on, OAuth flow, provider failover.
examples: No test launches Pluto_cli and sends input
No test verifies GUI window creation
No test exercises MCP stdio transport

hypothetical_findings.description: Single-platform (Haiku) with no CI on Haiku infrastructure. Cross-compilation mocks are hand-written and incomplete. No automated verification that macOS/Linux cross-build produces working Haiku binaries.
examples: build_haiku.sh rsyncs to a single hardcoded IP (192.168.1.34)
No GitHub Actions / GitLab CI / Buildbot on Haiku
Mock libs are .dylib (macOS) not .so (Linux) or Haiku .so

hypothetical_findings.description: Build time will scale poorly: 40+ core sources + 4 binaries + 21 tests all rebuild from scratch on any header change. No unity builds, no precompiled headers, no ccache integration.
examples: Change config.h → rebuilds all 65+ objects
No `make -j` optimization in CI target
CMake doesn't use target_sources for better incrementality

hypothetical_findings.description: Tight coupling between build system and Haiku private headers. 14 private header paths in CXXFLAGS. Any Haiku OS update breaks build. No abstraction layer or version detection.
examples: -I/boot/system/develop/headers/private/interface
-I/boot/system/develop/headers/private/kernel
src/compat/haiku/ duplicates public API surface

hypothetical_findings.description: Dual build systems (Makefile + CMake) maintained in parallel. CMake is 454 lines, Makefile 387 lines. Both must be kept in sync. Veterans would pick one (CMake for cross-platform, Makefile for Haiku-only).
examples: Both define same sources, flags, targets
CMake has mock pkg-config logic, Makefile has mock libs
Recipe uses Make, toolchain uses CMake

hypothetical_findings.description: Build knowledge concentrated in Makefile author. No documentation on: how to add a test, how to add a source file, how cross-compilation works, how to update mock headers, how to build HPKG.
examples: Adding a test requires editing TEST_BINS, adding rule, understanding mock deps
No BUILD.md or CONTRIBUTING.md with build instructions
Mock header generation process undocumented

hypothetical_findings.description: Mock headers leak into source via `-Isrc/compat/haiku` and `-Imock_headers/haiku`. Source code sees mock types (BMessage, BPath) identically to real Haiku types — but behavior differs (all methods return B_ERROR). Subtle bugs when logic depends on return values.
examples: BMessage::FindString always returns B_ERROR in mock
BNode::ReadAttr always returns -1 in mock
Tests pass on mock but fail on real Haiku

hypothetical_findings.description: Makefile.backup (15K) sits in root — indicates major rewrite without cleanup. .d dependency files and .o objects checked in (test_*.d, test_*.o). Build artifacts in repo root pollute git status.
examples: Makefile.backup 15K lines
test_json.d, test_json.o, test_loop-*.o.tmp in root
.gitignore doesn't ignore *.d, *.o, *.dylib

hypothetical_findings.description: Developer experience friction: no `make debug`, no `make test_json` (only `make check` runs all), no `make run-cli`, no `make run-gui`. Version defined in 3 places (Makefile, version.h, recipe).
examples: PKG_VERSION=0.7.1 (Makefile) vs PLUTO_VERSION=0.7.1 (version.h) vs $portVersion (recipe)
No IDE integration (compile_commands.json not generated by Makefile)
install.sh has wrong version

top_5_concerns: Cross-compilation mocks are incomplete and untested — no CI validates they produce working Haiku binaries
Zero integration/e2e tests — only unit tests for isolated functions
Dual build systems (Makefile + CMake) diverge silently — maintenance burden
Haiku private header dependency — any OS update breaks build
No automated CI on Haiku infrastructure — single manual rsync script to one IP
architecture_smells: Mock headers as leaky abstraction: source compiles against mocks but tests don't run on real Haiku in CI
Build system encodes platform assumptions (Hardcoded paths, Homebrew, private SDK) instead of discovering them
praise: Self-contained test binaries with no framework dependency — fast, simple, debuggable
Comprehensive benchmark suite (bench.cpp) with microbenchmarks for JSON, RAG, markdown, memory
HaikuPorts recipe follows conventions (BUILD/INSTALL/TEST phases, proper dependencies)
Resource file (pluto.rsrc) built from .rdef + .hvif via standard Haiku tools (rc/xres/addattr)
Version.h provides single-source version for runtime user-agent string
veteran_quotes: "Thirty years of shipping games taught me: if you can't cross-compile and run tests on the target platform in CI, you don't have a build system — you have a wish list. This mock layer? It's a Potemkin village. Looks like a build from the outside, collapses when you touch it." — 28-year engine veteran

"I've seen this dual Makefile/CMake pattern kill projects. Team splits: 'Makefile works on Haiku!' 'CMake works on Linux!' Neither works everywhere. Pick one. If Haiku-only, Makefile is fine. If cross-platform, CMake. Maintaining both is technical bankruptcy." — 22-year tools programmer

"The test suite is unit-test theater. 21 binaries testing parsers and helpers — but zero tests that launch the actual app, send a message, verify the GUI updates. That's where bugs live. In 2005 we called this 'testing the pavement, not the car.'" — 25-year QA lead
